IMPORTANT NOTICES
The Company holds cryptocurrencies or crypto assets in its treasury. Whilst the Board of Directors of the Company considers holding cryptocurrencies to be in the best interests of the Company, the Board remains aware that the financial regulator in the UK (the Financial Conduct Authority or FCA) considers investment in cryptocurrencies to be high risk. At the outset, it is important to note that an investment in the Company is not an investment in cryptocurrencies, either directly or by proxy and shareholders will have no direct access to the Company's holdings. However, the Board of Directors consider cryptocurrencies to be an appropriate store of value and potential growth and therefore appropriate for the Company. Accordingly, the Company is and intends to continue to be materially exposed to cryptocurrencies.
The Company is neither authorised nor regulated by the FCA, and the purchase of certain cryptocurrencies are generally unregulated in the UK. As with most other investments, the value of cryptocurrencies can go down as well as up, and therefore the value of the Company's cryptocurrencies holdings can fluctuate. The Company may not be able to realise its cryptocurrencies holdings for the same as it paid to acquire them or even for the value the Company currently ascribes to its cryptocurrencies positions due to market movements. Neither the Company nor investors in the Company's shares are protected by the UK's Financial Ombudsman Service or the Financial Services Compensation Scheme.
Cryptocurrencies may present special risks to the Company's financial position. These risks include (but are not limited to): (i) the value of cryptocurrencies can be highly volatile, with value dropping as quickly as it can rise. Investors in cryptocurrencies must be prepared to lose all money invested in cryptocurrencies; (ii) the cryptocurrencies market is largely unregulated. There is a risk of losing money due to risks such as cyber-attacks, financial crime and counterparty failure; (iii) the Company may not be able to sell its cryptocurrencies at will. The ability to sell cryptocurrencies depends on various factors, including the supply and demand in the market at the relevant time. Operational failings such as technology outages, cyber-attacks and commingling of funds could cause unwanted delay; and (iv) crypto assets are characterised in some quarters by high degrees of fraud, money laundering and financial crime. Prospective investors in the Company are encouraged to do their own research before investing.
The Company also holds digital tokens as part of its strategy to become the global market leader in the rapidly developing tokenised digital markets sector. Whilst the Board of Directors of the Company considers holding tokens to be in the best interests of the Company, it is important to note that an investment in the Company is not a direct or indirect ownership interest, security, or claim in respect of any underlying asset or reserve to which a token may relate. The valuation of tokens, particularly those linked to mining reserves or other physical assets, is inherently uncertain and may depend on independent third-party verification. Further risks include the liquidity of the tokenised markets, reliance on the security and continued operation of underlying blockchain or smart contract infrastructure, counterparty and custody risk in respect of third party platforms, the risk of misrepresentation or fraud regarding underlying reserves, and evolving regulatory, tax, and accounting treatment. Quorium Global Photonics SPC ("QGP") Update
Valereum Plc (AQSE: VLRM | OTCQB: VLRMF), a company aiming to become the global market leader in the tokenised digital markets sector,
is pleased to share an update on the Definitive Agreement with Quorium Global Photonics SPC ("QGP").
Valereum announces that QGP has issued
$VXRUP
, a stablecoin natively on
Ripple's XRP Ledger
("XRPL"), as the primary liquidity vehicle for its ecosystem.
QGP has notified the Company that the $VXRUP stablecoin issuance is the foundation of their liquidity framework, and a significant step towards the completion of the transaction and execution of the Company's digital asset strategy.
Further details are provided on the newsroom of QGP's website at
https://qgphotonics.com/newsroom
In the meantime, the Company continues to hold the tokens under the original agreement announced on 29 January 2026 being the 20,000 QMTN2601001 medium term notes at a value of $10,000 per token. The valuation of tokens is inherently uncertain, and investors are reminded to read the important notices section of this announcement and future announcements before making an investment decision.
Further updates will be made as required.
James Bannon, Chair of Valereum Plc, commented:
"To coin a phrase, Rome wasn't built in a day. This has been a highly complex undertaking and is, for QGP, already 3 years in the making. We are in the final stages of building something groundbreaking that will put Valereum at the forefront of securitised digital banking. The Board remains committed to ensuring institutional-grade liquidity, and moving to completion with the crucial legitimacy in place."
Gary Cottle, Group CEO, adds:
"While this has taken longer than anticipated, we are hopeful the end result is significantly improved than when we first set out our roadmap."
Pieter Scholtz, Managing Director of QGP-SPC, commented:
"This is the moment we move from preparation to execution. The pieces are assembled. The infrastructure is operational. The pathway to liquidity is clear. QGP is proud to contribute its assets and expertise to this partnership - real assets and real infrastructure."

Valereum Plc
("Valereum", "VLRM" or the "Company")
Announces pan African and Indian Ocean
Digital Asset Strategic Partnership with Blockchain Digital Assets Limited (Africa)
Valereum Plc (AQSE: VLRM | OTCQB: VLRMF), a company aiming to become the global market leader in the rapidly developing tokenised digital markets sector, is pleased to announce that it has entered into an agreement with Blockchain Digital Assets Limited (Africa) (known as "BDAL" or "Koinon"), a specialist advisory and digital asset business with extensive relationships across Africa and the Indian Ocean.
The partnership brings together Valereum's regulated digital asset ecosystem, tokenisation capabilities and payments infrastructure with BDAL's regional expertise and commercial relationships to accelerate the adoption of digital assets in multiple high-growth markets.
The joint venture will initially focus on three areas:
1.
Real World Asset Tokenisation
- focusing on land extraction tokenisation (gold, platinum, lithium etc), leveraging the VLRM Markets platform (powered by DigiShares) and gold yield-bearing tokenisation ecosystem. A joint offering will advance BDAL's access to the listed exchanges across the African region.
2.
Digital Payments
- expanding across Africa leveraging the mobile application Koinon has developed with its Interswitch and Pipechain payments hub, and integrating the various Valereum white label payments platforms. A full on- and off-ramp white-label solution can offer AI payment solutions that support both B2B2C and B2C audiences.
3.
TradFi/Digital Banking Infrastructure
- exploring opportunities to develop next-generation digital banking services across Africa by combining advisory expertise, regulated digital asset infrastructure and execution platforms to deliver an integrated suite of financial products.
About Blockchain Digital Assets Limited (Africa)
Blockchain Digital Assets Limited (Africa) (BDAL), a Kenyan registered entity, is a specialist advisory business focused on digital assets, payments and financial infrastructure across Africa and the Indian Ocean. The company has developed an extensive regional network spanning government, financial institutions and private enterprise, supporting projects across digital payments, tokenisation and financial services innovation.
Matthew Mecke, Founder and Managing Partner of BDAL, commented:
"
It's a natural choice for us to work with the Valereum team, given how similar our roadmaps are. We've spent three decades building deep relationships across the continent and firmly believe there will be a significant adoption of digital banking across Africa at a product and client level
."
Gary Cottle, Group CEO of Valereum Plc, added:
"
This is an obvious geographical and product extension to our business model and aspirations. In the same way, it makes more sense for BDAL to leverage our platforms and ecosystem (rather than build their own). The degree of expertise and market knowledge that Matthew and his team can bring to bear is immense and we're looking forward to working together to speed up their Go To Market strategy."

company_30s.what_they_do: VLRM is a niche tech firm that builds photonics‑based data‑transmission equipment and also runs a digital‑asset platform for secure, high‑speed transactions.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The digital‑asset market is expanding rapidly and photonics solutions are essential for next‑generation data centers. VLRM sits at the intersection of these two high‑growth arenas, offering a potentially scalable product line.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still in an early‑stage growth phase, having just raised £1.05 million and released a fresh set of product updates. Its stock is trading at a very low level, a steep drop from previous highs, and the company is still building revenue streams.

rns_narrative: VLRM has been busy announcing a new digital‑asset partnership and updating its photonics product line. A fresh issue of its media arm, Valereum Vox, was released, and it published quarterly results that show modest earnings. The company also raised fresh capital and disclosed holdings that hint at strategic moves.

These events cluster around two themes: (1) a pivot toward digital‑asset infrastructure backed by strategic partnerships, and (2) continued investment in photonics technology to support high‑speed data transmission.
There are signs the company is stabilising its product roadmap, but it still needs a clear revenue driver. The lack of a clear catalyst yet gives the stock a high surprise potential.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet in the crowd, but a storm brewing
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls see the digital‑asset partnership as a doorway to new revenue streams and the photonics line as a high‑margin product.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that VLRM’s thin track record and heavy reliance on capital raises could stall growth, and that the photonics niche may not scale.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: No chatter has surfaced yet, but the silence is a classic contrarian signal that the market has overlooked the company’s potential.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends are flat – no public buzz, which is a green flag for a contrarian play.

near_term_catalysts: A Q3 earnings report that shows positive revenue growth or a clear path to profitability.
The announcement of a new partnership with a major digital‑asset exchange or a large data‑center client for the photonics platform.
A fresh funding round that signals confidence from institutional investors.
A breakout from the 20‑day moving average with volume at least twice the 20‑day average.
expect_next.watch_for: A sudden spike in daily volume, a price break above the 50‑day SMA, or a positive earnings release. These would confirm that the market has accepted the company’s pivot and that a mean‑reversion bounce is likely.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a post‑crash recovery. The APEX score indicates tight compression, suggesting a potential breakout is imminent once a catalyst confirms the business model.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If VLRM recovers to halfway between its current price and all‑time high, the upside is roughly 36% of the current level. Historically, a green signal yields about a 39% return with a 40% win rate, meaning a reward that far outweighs the 100% risk of a full wipe‑out. Even a modest bounce to 70% of the ATH would deliver a 56% upside.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company has no proven revenue track record and relies on fresh capital raises that may not convert to growth. If the digital‑asset partnership fails to materialise or the photonics line remains niche, the stock could fall to zero.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Risk: 100% down to zero. Reward: 70% if it hits the all‑time high, 36% if it reaches halfway. Reward/risk ratio is about 0.36–0.7, a classic high‑asymmetry contrarian trade.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a breakout above the 20‑day SMA with volume >2× the 20‑day average. Allocate 5–10% of the discretionary portfolio. Place a stop just below the 20‑day SMA and trail the stop as the price rises.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a volume spike and a positive earnings release or a new partnership announcement. If the stock breaks above the 50‑day SMA with volume >3× the 20‑day average, consider entering.
playbook.if_passing: No genuine terminal risks are evident; the trade remains bullish on a deep‑crashed setup with potential catalysts.

ai_insights.bottom_line: A deep crash, silent crowd and upcoming partnership announcements create a high‑asymmetry contrarian play that could pay off if the stock rebounds to halfway between its current level and all‑time high.
